P1.question: how did each paper obtain a target signature at all
P1.answer: Four routes, all now read at the source. (1) BUILD IT ON THE STACK: Sagitta and Monte-Carlo SBR both write their own PO/MECA integrator over a graphics tracer - and MC-SBR says in one sentence that Mitsuba has no surface-current or PO support, which is the published version of our P1 claim and the justification for our architecture. (2) EXTEND THE ENGINE'S RAY PHYSICS: Ziganshin, on Sionna-RT v0.19, keeps everything inside the ray formalism and buys the missing field with diffraction coefficients. (3) BUY IT: LAMBDA queries a CADFEKO RCS file by UAV attitude and multiplies it into every path. (4) MEASURE IT: Costa builds a bistatic reflectivity library S21(f) of a real drone body and injects it.
P1.the_gap_that_is_still_ours: route (1) has never been applied to a drone by anyone in this archive, and routes (3) and (4) both collapse the signature to something less than a per-path bistatic quantity.

P2.question: where did each paper get its target material values, and did it cite a measurement
P2.answer: Nobody sourced a TARGET material from a measurement. Three papers do something better than guessing: Hoydis makes (sigma, eps_r, S, K_x) differentiable and fits them to channel measurements, and MEASURES the penalty for not doing so - 4.93 dB mean absolute level error with the stock ITU table, 2.16 dB after calibration, 1.00 dB with position-dependent neural materials. MC-SBR replaces a scalar reflection coefficient with MECA equivalent currents derived from the material constants. jees2021 collapses carbon fibre to PEC and CITES two papers showing the dynamic RCS is nearly identical. Against those, md-rt's stock 'Wood' propeller and Costa's hand-tuned body ratio are weaker than our own annotated values.
P2.actionable: the Hoydis route is directly available to us: our kernel is already differentiable in Mitsuba, and the X410 campaign will produce the measurements. ⛔[정정 2026-09-05] what Hoydis MEASURED is an indoor PROPAGATION-CHANNEL calibration - a 3.438 GHz hallway at Stuttgart, mean absolute channel-gain level error (ALE) 4.93 dB with the stock ITU table (its std is 5.26 dB), 2.16 dB after gradient calibration, 1.00 dB with position-dependent neural materials. The 2.7-3.9 dB is OUR ARITHMETIC on those three numbers (4.93-2.16 and 4.93-1.00), not a gain anyone published, and nothing in that paper says a TARGET-material calibration for our drone RCS buys the same amount. Quote the three ALE values with their indoor-channel context; do not quote 2.7-3.9 dB as our expected gain.

P3.question: who else met this, and did anyone express rotation INSIDE the engine
P3.answer: Nobody expressed rotation inside the engine. Two credible workarounds exist and we should say which one we use and why. (a) ANALYTIC: Costa keeps rotation entirely in the signal model with a closed-form bistatic thin-wire integral, which is exact for a wire, free of any tracer, and validated against measurement at r = 0.98 - but it cannot carry shape or shadowing. (b) RE-POSE PER PHASE: jees2021 does exactly what our pose_articulated() does, in MoM, and makes it 157x cheaper by never rebuilding the impedance matrix (rotate the incidence direction instead of the propeller) and by deriving the CCW propeller from the CW one by a sign flip on the cross-polar terms. The published phase count for a revolution in this literature is 512.
P3.actionable: the jees invariance trick maps onto our PO kernel: for a blade sub-mesh, rotating the blade equals counter-rotating the incident direction in the blade frame, so facet areas and local normals never need rebuilding - only the incidence vector and the hub phase.

P4.question: who closed the diffraction gap, what did it cost, what did it buy, is any of it usable by us
P4.answer: TWO FAMILIES. UTD family (Ziganshin): buys shadow-region field where a specular-only method returns nothing, at 15-27x runtime, with a residual MAE of 1.6-3.0 dB; it is architecturally incompatible with our PO kernel because it replaces rather than corrects the surface integral, and neither of his documents contains a frequency sweep, so it is NOT evidence about our band slope. PTD family (Kirik-Ozdemir algorithm, Ozturk derivation): an ADDITIVE fringe correction, E_tot = E_PTDEEC + E_PO, computed per ray whose hit point falls within lambda/10 of a detected convex edge, with an equivalent edge length dl = (1/rho_rd) d_max (cos t_i1 + cos t_i2). That is the one that bolts onto what we already have.
P4.the_experiment_that_settles_our_slope: Kirik-Ozdemir ran it: the same monostatic sweep 7.5-12.5 GHz at 100 points, with and without PTD, then IFFT to a range profile to confirm the added energy sits at the edges. They report it only as a figure with no dB values, so the number we need does not exist in the literature - we have to run it ourselves.
P4.honesty: our own arithmetic (in outputs/psolve_diffraction.json) predicts a frequency-flat edge term cannot by itself close a 3.5-8x slope excess. Nothing in this deep read contradicts that, and nothing supports it either. The with/without sweep is the falsifiable test.

P5.question: who validated an absolute level, against what reference, and to what accuracy
P5.answer: The best answers are in the measurement papers, not the simulation papers. Das anchors to a machined 2.8 dBsm cylinder through a three-measurement chain (background, calibration body, target) with coherent background subtraction, sixth-order Kaiser range gating and a peak-power ratio, citing IEEE Std 1502-2020. Zhang anchors to a 0.5 m sphere and reports the residual: theory -7.07 dBsm, measured -8.96 dBsm, under 2 dB. On the simulation side: Sagitta gets within +/-2% of analytical Mie; MC-SBR gets within 0.01 dBsm^2 of deterministic SBR above 10 rays/lambda and within 1-2 dB overall; Ziganshin's only absolute comparison against measurement he calls qualitative.
P5.the_number_to_carry: about 2 dB is what a careful chamber chain achieves on a canonical body. Any absolute claim we make should be quoted with an uncertainty no smaller than that, and we currently have none at all.

P7.question: did anyone state a validity floor for their high-frequency approximation, or check it
P7.answer: One paper states a number and proves it: Sagitta sweeps a PEC sphere against Mie across four decades of electrical size and finds the optical region begins at kr ~ 30 with about 2.5% standard deviation, with an upper aliasing bound at kr ~ 8e3 for a fixed ray grid. Ozturk's thesis gives the same story for the EDGE term, measured on discs at ka = 5, 10, 15: agreement improves with radius because a small disc lets the fringe current re-diffract. Zhang states the ka taxonomy without a number. Ziganshin substitutes a FACET-size rule (E > 1.5 lambda) for a target-size rule, which is a different constraint.
P7.consequence_for_us: we now have three independent, citable floors of different kinds - target electrical size (kr), facet edge length (E > 1.5 lambda), and ray-grid spacing (lambda/5 or 10 rays/lambda). We should state all three for every airframe and every band, and name the ones we fail.

P8.question: who computed bistatic scattering in a ray engine, and did they check reciprocity or symmetry
P8.answer: Ziganshin computed it (both documents, all bistatic angles, near and far field) and never checked reciprocity. Sagitta declined to compute it and said why, in footnote 1 on p4: a bistatic calculation needs a visibility function for shadowing between the reflection points and the receiver, which the monostatic case can omit because the scattering surfaces are by assumption visible to the co-located launcher and receiver. That footnote is the published diagnosis of our exit-visibility effect. Nobody in this file ran a reciprocity or symmetry test on their own scattering kernel.
P8.what_the_measurements_say_about_the_bist: Das: monostatic mean RCS is consistently the highest, and going to 90 deg bistatic costs only about 1-2 dB of mean target path loss while frequency costs 3-15 dB and platform type up to 30 dB. Costa measured a full drone bistatic reflectivity surface from 10 to 180 deg at 5.78-8.22 GHz. So the bistatic dimension is real but shallow in the mean - which makes our beta <= 45 deg restriction cheap to defend and cheap to test.

equations_as_printed_appendix_A.note: Appendix A gives the STRUCTURE of the coefficients, not full expressions. To reimplement you must go to refs [21][22][23]; the paper is explicit that it only 'emphasiz[es] the structure of the diffraction coefficients and associated transition functions'.
equations_as_printed_appendix_A.edge_UTD_eq1: D_E ~ sum_{i=1..4} cot( Phi_i / 2n ) F(a_i);  Phi = pi +/- (phi -/+ phi'); wedge angle = (2-n)pi; F = UTD transition function
equations_as_printed_appendix_A.vertex_eq2: D_V ~ sum_{i=1..4} B(Phi_i) T_GFI(b, a_i);  cot replaced by trigonometric B(Phi); T_GFI = Generalized Fresnel Integral; b = optical distance between vertex and edge rays, a as in edge case
equations_as_printed_appendix_A.double_edge_eq3: D~_EE ~ sum_{i,j} cot(Phi_1i/2n1) cot(Phi_2j/2n2) T~(a_i,b_j,w)   [hard component]
equations_as_printed_appendix_A.double_edge_eq4: D~~_EE ~ sum_{i,j} csc^2(Phi_1i/2n1) csc^2(Phi_2j/2n2) T~~(a_i,b_j,w)   [soft component; asymptotically weaker OUTSIDE transition regions but same order near double transitions]
equations_as_printed_appendix_A.edge_vertex_eq5: D_EV ~ sum_{i,j} cot(Phi_1i/2n1) B(Phi_2j) T_EV(a_i, b, c_j, w)
equations_as_printed_appendix_A.the_heuristic_rule_verbatim_structure: T_EV outside the transition region = F(a)*T_GFI(c,b); close to the edge transition = F(a)*T_GFI(c, b/sqrt(1-w^2)); LINEAR INTERPOLATION between the two regimes
equations_as_printed_appendix_A.stated_limitation_of_the_heuristic: EV/VE chaining can only describe the HARD diffraction component; the soft component cannot be represented

method_what_they_actually_implemented.pipeline: trace-then-integrate, four stages: (1) orthographic ray grid sampling, (2) BVH-accelerated intersection queries, (3) iterative multi-bounce transport writing a compact hit record, (4) PO accumulation as a reduction over VALID hit records only
method_what_they_actually_implemented.ray_launch: for each incident direction (theta,phi) an ORTHOGRAPHIC bundle from a virtual aperture plane orthogonal to k_inc; basis {u,v,k_inc}; aperture extents L_u, L_v from projecting the 8 corners of the mesh AABB onto u and v, inflated by (1+eta); Cartesian grid with spacing ds; N_rays = ceil(Lu~/ds)*ceil(Lv~/ds); each ray carries area weight dA = ds^2
method_what_they_actually_implemented.PO_sum_eq7: A = sum_i  [ j*k*dA/(4*pi) ] * 2 * ( n_i . (-k_inc) ) * Gamma^{N_i} * exp(-j*2*k*R_i);  sigma = 4*pi*|A|^2, reported as 10log10(sigma) dBsm
method_what_they_actually_implemented.symbol_meanings: n_i = surface normal at the FIRST interaction; R_i = accumulated optical path length INCLUDING reflections; N_i = number of reflections; Gamma = a reflection coefficient that may depend on polarization and incidence angle, raised to the power of the bounce count
method_what_they_actually_implemented.PO_current: J_s = 2 n x H_inc on the lit region, 0 in shadow (tangent-plane approximation); far field via Stratton-Chu
method_what_they_actually_implemented.no_spreading_factors: 'Rather than tracking ray tube divergence through spreading factors, we control integration error through the density of the incident ray grid' - accuracy is converted into a pure resolution requirement
method_what_they_actually_implemented.traversal: explicit fixed-size stack, no recursion; specular update d_new = d - 2(d.n)n; origin offset by epsilon along the normal to avoid self-intersection; B_max bounces (100 used for the aircraft, to capture engine intakes)
method_what_they_actually_implemented.BVH: built once per mesh, reused for all angles; two split rules: median-of-centroids along the longest AABB axis, or binned Surface Area Heuristic C_SAH = C_T + (SA(L)/SA(P))*N_L*C_I + (SA(R)/SA(P))*N_R*C_I; nodes linearised preorder; leaves reference contiguous triangle ranges; built with OpenMP tasks and an atomic node pool
method_what_they_actually_implemented.parallelism: angular sweep distributed across MPI ranks (embarrassingly parallel); every rank holds the full mesh + BVH, so problem size is bounded by ONE GPU's memory

the_sampling_rule_we_should_adopt_or_ref.rule: ds <= lambda/5, i.e. at least five ray samples per wavelength across the incident aperture
the_sampling_rule_we_should_adopt_or_ref.failure_mode_it_prevents: spatial ALIASING of the phase term in the discrete PO sum, which shows up as non-physical oscillations and incorrect nulls in the RCS pattern - and which they warn is routinely MISDIAGNOSED as floating-point precision loss
the_sampling_rule_we_should_adopt_or_ref.cost_law: ray count grows O(ds^-2), quadratic in frequency
the_sampling_rule_we_should_adopt_or_ref.empirical_proof: holding the grid fixed through a frequency sweep, the lambda/5 criterion is eventually violated and an aliasing instability appears at kr ~ 8e3
the_sampling_rule_we_should_adopt_or_ref.note_vs_MC_SBR: the Monte-Carlo SBR paper independently recommends 10 rays per wavelength for its strata - a factor 2 stricter

validity_floor_P7.statement: 'good agreement typically expected for kr >~ 30'; their own sweep shows excellent agreement with Mie 'beginning at an electrical size around kr ~ 30'
validity_floor_P7.tolerance_attached: ~2.5% standard deviation in the optical region, and 'within +/-2% of the analytical solution' over more than two orders of magnitude in electrical size
validity_floor_P7.upper_bound: aliasing instability at kr ~ 8e3 with a fixed grid; they also state SBR is intended for kr <~ 1e5
validity_floor_P7.how_this_relates_to_OUR_kr_9.06: NOT A CONTRADICTION. Their floor is for a ~2% amplitude tolerance (about 0.17 dB); ours is for a 1 dB tolerance (26% in power). A tighter tolerance necessarily pushes the floor up. If we ever want to claim ~0.2 dB fidelity we must use their kr>=30, and mini5pro at LTE (kr 8.4) fails that by a factor of 3.6.
validity_floor_P7.validation_config: PEC sphere, 22,000 x 22,000 ray grid from a square aperture 2.05 m on a side; r = 1 m corresponds to ~1 GHz to ~300 GHz

runtime_and_hardware.flagship: A380, 162,000 triangles, 80x73x21 m, 10 GHz (lambda ~ 3 cm), 30,000 x 30,000 rays from a 90x90 m aperture, max 100 reflections, 500 phi x 250 theta = 125,000 angles, 1.125e14 rays total; 616.12 ms per angular position in FP32; total sweep ~27 minutes on 8 LUMI nodes (4 AMD MI250X per node)

kernel_split_table_I.scene: A380, 18,000 x 18,000 rays, 1 MPI process, 10 repetitions of a 600-angle scan
kernel_split_table_I.reading: the PO integral is 3-5% of the cost; intersection dominates. Our own optimisation effort should go to the tracer, not the integral.

runtime_and_hardware.scaling: strong ~88% at 256 GCDs; weak ~96%; base workload 45,000 x 45,000 rays per node
runtime_and_hardware.efficiency_note: only 5-10% of launched rays hit the target at typical aspects; they accept the waste rather than pre-filter
runtime_and_hardware.precision_finding: FP32 accumulates ~2-3% phase error after 100 reflections through catastrophic cancellation in exp(-j2kR); acceptable on a dBsm scale. FP32 vs FP64 preference is architecture-dependent (FP32 on A100, FP64 on MI250X). FP32 results are also non-deterministic run to run; they recommend repeating and averaging.

what_they_did_NOT_do_and_said_so: no diffraction of any kind - GTD/UTD/PTD listed as future work
no dielectrics, no full polarimetry - listed as future work

monostatic only, and the reason is stated in footnote 1 on p4: a bistatic calculation needs a VISIBILITY FUNCTION for shadowing between the reflection points and the receiver, which the monostatic case lets you skip because the scattering surfaces are by assumption visible to the co-located launcher/receiver
why_this_is_the_most_important_row_for_u: It is an independent, code-released implementation of exactly our kernel structure (GO+PO SBR, Gamma^N, exp(-j2kR), sigma=4pi|A|^2), which means our architecture is defensible by citation rather than by assertion.

Its footnote 1 is the published statement of OUR P8 problem: bistatic SBR needs an exit-visibility test. Our own multistatic check found an exit-visibility effect; this is the citation for why it exists.
It gives us a numeric sampling rule (lambda/5) and a numeric validity floor (kr>=30 at 2%) that we can either meet or explicitly declare we do not meet.
It gives the GPU cost of the honest version of our method at scale, so our own runtime can be positioned rather than floated.

step_i_edge_detection: find neighbouring triangular patches sharing at least two vertices
compute the outward normals of both patches; if the normals DIVERGE the edge is outward-directed and enters the PTD sum (convex edges only)
apply a maximum edge-angle threshold, 'usually selected as 30 deg in practice in order not to have almost zero PTD contribution energy'
the_algorithm_verbatim_structure.step_ii_ray_to_edge_distance: d_hit = |(P0-P1) x (P0-P2)| / |P2-P1|, with P0 the ray-hit point and P1,P2 the edge endpoints (perpendicular distance from the hit point to the edge line)

step_iii_inclusion_test_and_equivalent_l.test: include this ray's diffraction contribution iff d_hit <= d_max = lambda/10  (cited as a rule of thumb from Weinmann TAP 2006)
step_iii_inclusion_test_and_equivalent_l.rho_rd: the ray density of the SBR ray bunch, 'usually taken as one-tenth of the operational wavelength' i.e. 10 rays per wavelength
step_iii_inclusion_test_and_equivalent_l.theta_i1, theta_i2: the ray incidence angles measured against the two faces of the wedge

the_algorithm_verbatim_structure.step_iv_diffracted_field: E_d = [exp(-jk|r-r'|)/(2 pi |r-r'|)] * dl * { (D_m - D'_perp)(E_i . a_i,par) a_s,perp  -  (D_e - D'_par)(sin b_s/sin b_i)(E_i . a_i,par) a_s,par  -  (D_em sin(b') - D'_x)(sin b_s/sin b_i)(E_i . a_i,perp) a_s,par }
the_algorithm_verbatim_structure.unit_vectors: a_i,perp = (t x i)/|t x i|, a_i,par = i x a_i,perp ; a_s,perp = (t x s)/|t x s|, a_s,par = s x a_s,perp ; t = edge direction unit vector, i and s the incident and scattered ray directions; b_i, b_s the incidence/scattering angles measured from t
the_algorithm_verbatim_structure.coefficients: D_e, D_m, D_em are the wedge diffraction coefficients (eq 5a) written in terms of n (wedge angle alpha = n*pi), theta_i, theta_s and the auxiliary angles alpha1, alpha2; D'_perp, D'_par, D'_x are the PO-based coefficients (eq 5b): D'_perp = -sin(theta_s)/(cos(alpha1)+cos(theta_i)), D'_par = -sin(theta_i)/(cos(alpha1)+cos(theta_i)), D'_x = -K cos(theta_s)/(cos(alpha1)+cos(theta_i))
the_algorithm_verbatim_structure.auxiliaries_eq6: K = sin(b_s) cot(b_i) - sin(b_i) cot(b_s);  sin(alpha1) = sqrt(sin^2 b_i - sin^2 b_i cos^2 theta_s)/sin(b_i);  sin(alpha2) = sqrt(sin^2 b_i - sin^2 b_s cos^2(n pi - theta_s))/sin(b_i)
the_algorithm_verbatim_structure.the_essential_idea: the SUBTRACTION D - D' is the fringe (PTD) correction: the full wedge coefficient minus its PO part, so that adding E_d to the PO surface integral does not double count.
the_algorithm_verbatim_structure.implementation: coded in C# / .NET as a module of the Predics (pRediCS) GO-PO ray launcher

method.family: Method of Equivalent Edge Currents (EEC). Fringe-wave currents from Michaeli's surface-current-based formulation.
method.decomposition: the surface current is split into a PO part and a non-uniform FRINGE-WAVE part; the fringe part is the correction, so PO-EEC gives the PO diffracted field and PTD-EEC gives the fringe-wave diffracted field
method.combination_rule_eq_3_42: E_tot = E_PTDEEC + E_PO - the edge-diffracted field is ADDED to the PO surface integral computed by the same program. This is the architecture that is compatible with our kernel.
method.backscattering_simplification: for monostatic, beta = pi - beta', phi = phi'; then alpha1 = arccos(cos phi - 2 cot^2 beta) and alpha2 = arccos(cos(N pi - phi) - 2 cot^2 beta) (eqs 3.35/3.36), and the fringe current densities I^f (3.37) and M^f (3.38) written with these are SINGULARITY-FREE except in degenerate cases - which is why they are the ones coded
method.square_plate_specialisation: with beta' = phi' = pi/2 and N = 2 the currents collapse to eqs (3.39)/(3.40) with mu = sin(beta) cos(phi)
method.order: FIRST-ORDER diffraction only; the fringe current is assumed to travel to infinity as on a half plane, so re-diffraction at a second edge is neglected. The thesis says this can be mitigated by using a larger plate.

P3_how_rotation_is_expressed.model: thin-wire: each blade is a rigid homogeneous line of infinitely many point scatterers from the hub to the tip, integrated in closed form
P3_how_rotation_is_expressed.bistatic_range_of_a_rotating_point: R_P(t) ~= R_O - A_B * l * cos(omega t + phi_B), with A_B = sqrt(4 cos^2(beta/2) - (cos beta_T + cos beta_R)^2) and phi_B = phi_T - arctan[ sin(beta_R) sin(phi_T - phi_R) / (sin beta_T + sin beta_R cos(phi_T - phi_R)) ]
P3_how_rotation_is_expressed.no_restriction: the formulation places NO restriction on the orientation of the rotation plane relative to Tx/Rx - which is exactly the generality the older discrete-point bistatic model lacked
P3_how_rotation_is_expressed.HRR_extension: integrating only over the part of the blade whose delay falls in the current range bin gives limits l1, l2 taken as the MEDIAN of a three-element set, and the blade response becomes (l2-l1)/2 * sinc(omega_n/c * dR-) * exp(j omega_n/c * dR+), with dR+ = (l2+l1)/2 * psi and dR- = (l2-l1)/2 * psi, psi = A_B cos(omega t + phi_B)
P3_how_rotation_is_expressed.multi_propeller: each propeller p gets its own centre O_p, its own omega_p, its own initial phase phi_0p ~ U(0,2 pi), its own speed; beta_Tp and beta_Rp are recomputed per propeller from the dot products. VTOL with a propeller orthogonal to the others is shown as a case.
P3_how_rotation_is_expressed.OFDM: the model is written directly for an OFDM symbol grid, x(mu,m) = sum_n D(n,m) exp(j omega_n (m + mu/N) T), and the per-subcarrier response is derived, so the output is a delay-Doppler cube not a single-tone Doppler trace
P3_how_rotation_is_expressed.vibration: body vibration added as a random-walk range perturbation D_v(t) = D_v(t-1) + D0 * U(-1,1) - and the paper shows it is REQUIRED to reproduce the measured body return in the HRR case
P3_how_rotation_is_expressed.approximation_error_bound: the far-field linearisation of the bistatic range has upper bound Err <= (l^2/2)(1/R_T + 1/R_R); for l = 0.1655 m and R_T = R_R = 3.43 m this is <= 8 mm, i.e. 0.12% of the bistatic range

P1_how_the_BODY_signature_is_obtained_tw.option_B_measured_library: measure S21(f) = |E_scat|^2/|E_inc|^2 of the static drone over many aspect and bistatic angles, build a library, select the profile for the desired geometry and sample it at f_n. papers.title: Dynamic RCS Estimation according to Drone Movement Using the MoM and Far-Field Approximation
papers.authors: Dong-Yeob Lee, Jae-In Lee, Dong-Wook Seo (Korea Maritime and Ocean University)
papers.venue_status: Journal of Electromagnetic Engineering and Science 21(4):322-328, Sep 2021, DOI 10.26866/jees.2021.4.r.40. PUBLISHED.
blockers_faced: P3 - rotating blades, met head on
P2 - had to choose a propeller material and justified it with a citation

method.insight: a rotating rigid propeller does not change shape, so the MoM impedance matrix - which depends only on the mesh - is INVARIANT under rotation. Build the mesh and the impedance/admittance matrices ONCE; instead of rotating the propeller, rotate the incident field's azimuth backwards and let the change land in the excitation vector.
method.second_trick: drones carry mirror-image CW and CCW propellers. Their co-polar scattered fields are identical and their cross-polar fields differ by 180 deg: [S_tt, S_tp; S_pt, S_pp]_CW = [S_tt, -S_tp; -S_pt, S_pp]_CCW. So all four propellers follow from ONE simulated propeller.
method.third_trick: far-field superposition with per-propeller phase offsets: E_P1(t) = sum_n E_Tn(t; theta_P1, phi_P1) exp(-j 2 k . r_n), r_n the propeller centre position; then RCS = lim 4 pi R^2 |E|^2/|E_i|^2
method.arbitrary_aspect: changing observation azimuth does NOT require recomputation - only a shift of the rotation START angle, +phi_obs for CW propellers and -phi_obs for CCW, plus the updated wave vector
method.numerics: MoM with RWG basis functions and EFIE, implemented in MATLAB; because only a single propeller's impedance matrix is inverted, plain Gauss elimination is used rather than an iterative solver

papers.parameters: DJI Mavic 2 propeller CAD, 20.32 cm long = about 6.5*lambda at 9.65 GHz; carrier 9.65 GHz; PRF 20 kHz; single propeller rotating once per second sampled at 0.1 deg intervals for one second (3600 phases); four-propeller cases at 156.6 Hz and 125.3 Hz rotation; incidence elevation 45 deg, azimuth 0 deg and 70 deg. BODY NOT MODELLED - propellers only.
papers.P2_material_decision_with_a_citation: 'Because the dynamic RCSs of propellers with carbon fiber and a perfect electric conductor (PEC) are very similar in terms of RCS level and patterns [16, 17], the material of the propellers was simply assumed to be the PEC.' This is the cleanest published justification in the archive for collapsing a drone material choice, and it is exactly the kind of citation our gamma_po values lack.
papers.validation: against Altair FEKO - MoM solver for the single propeller, MLFMM for the four-propeller cases (MoM was too slow). Stated result: 'There was little deviation in the results' - NO ERROR NUMBER. The quantitative agreement shown is spectral: the first spectral peak lands at 313.2 Hz and 313.3 Hz for a 156.6 Hz rotation (exactly 2x, because both blade tips scatter) and at 250.6 Hz for 125.3 Hz.

runtime.hardware: Intel Core i7-8700 at 3.20 GHz, 64 GB RAM, MATLAB
runtime.scope: one rotating propeller, 3600 rotation angles at 9.65 GHz

papers.what_transfers_to_us: Our pose_articulated() rebuilds the whole mesh at every rotor phase. The same invariance applies to a PO/SBR kernel: for the propeller sub-mesh, rotating the blade about its own axis is identical to counter-rotating the incident direction in the blade frame, so the per-facet geometry (areas, normals in the local frame) never has to be rebuilt - only the incidence direction and the hub phase offset change. And the CW/CCW mirror relation halves the work again. Neither shortcut is in our code today.

We rather, implemented our own render[er] and utilized the lower level functionality such as GPU dispatch and random number generation.' (p7). This is an independent, citable confirmation that the Mitsuba/Dr.Jit stack underneath Sionna RT has no scattering integral and that writing your own PO layer on it is the accepted move - which is precisely our architecture.

method.core_idea: reformulate the SBR integral equations as a MONTE CARLO estimator and import variance-reduction machinery from photorealistic rendering (stratification, Russian roulette, Fresnel splitting), so the GPU runs a fixed pipeline instead of managing a recursive tree of reflected+refracted rays
method.why_deterministic_SBR_hurts_on_GPUs: complex ray-tube intersection needs explicit double-count handling when tubes overlap; tracing both reflected and refracted rays builds a recursive tree with unpredictable memory; and much of that work is spent on low-energy paths
method.MECA: Modified Equivalent Current Approximation extends the PO tangent-plane current to DIELECTRIC surfaces using the surface equivalence principle - both electric and magnetic equivalent currents from the Fresnel reflection of the incident field
method.convergence: Monte Carlo variance falls linearly with sample count so error falls as 1/sqrt(N), independent of dimensionality - which is why it wins as the dielectric nesting depth (and hence the integral's dimensionality) grows
method.implementation: built on the Mitsuba retargetable renderer over Dr.Jit with CUDA and OptiX; they use Mitsuba for Fresnel equations and ray-triangle intersection only

papers.authors: S. Kasdorf, B. Troksa, C. Key, J. Harmon, B. M. Notaros (Colorado State University)

papers.why_it_is_here_and_why_it_is_ruled_out: It is the most-cited recent work on 'SBR accuracy', so it looks like a P1/P4 lead. It is not. Its subject is the RECEPTION side of propagation SBR: rays are launched from a transmitter, each carries a growing reception cone, and the accuracy problem is choosing the cone angle so the cones tile the sphere without gaps (undercounting) or extra overlap (double counting). Our PO kernel launches an orthographic aperture grid at the target and integrates surface currents - there are no reception spheres and no double counting of wavefronts at a receiver. Their solution does not transfer.
papers.what_they_did_anyway: per-ray cone angle from the local neighbour set on a subdivided icosahedron (rather than one global maximum); an analytic optimal CONSTANT cone angle derived from the inscribed-sphere radius of a regular icosahedron via the golden ratio; and a double-count removal that exploits the fact that overlapping cones can only be ADJACENT rays, so the search is a neighbour-set lookup instead of a path-history search or a distance query.

THE_NUMBER_THAT_MATTERS_FOR_P2.reading: using the STOCK ITU material table costs about 4.9 dB of mean absolute level error in a real indoor scene. the_join_read_precisely.what_the_tracer_gives: path-level records from Sionna RT: complex path gains, delays, Doppler shifts, angles of departure and arrival, interaction labels, UAV position and velocity
the_join_read_precisely.what_CADFEKO_gives: a UAV RCS file for the AirSim UAV model
the_join_read_precisely.how_they_are_combined: the radar synthesis multiplies, per valid path, the complex CSI coefficient by the two-way delay, the Doppler shift, the virtual-array steering phase and a UAV-ORIENTATION-DEPENDENT RCS, plus optional receiver noise, to form a dechirped FMCW radar cube
the_join_read_precisely.THE_LIMITATION_THIS_EXPOSES: the RCS is 'queried according to the UAV attitude' - one scalar per attitude, applied to every path. It is NOT indexed by the per-path bistatic angle pair. So the injected signature carries the target's orientation but not the geometry of each individual illumination/observation direction. Anyone who wants a truly bistatic signature cannot get it this way.
the_join_read_precisely.why_it_matters_to_us: our SBR+PO computes a signature per illumination/observation pair, which is strictly more than an attitude-indexed lookup can express. That is a concrete, defensible advantage over the only injection pipeline in the corpus - provided our bistatic window is honest (P8).
